title: Session 41 - AMS / Application Support Mission Pack
executiveSummary: Two applications were discussed. PG RegDoc has business, role, document-flow and high-level Azure evidence; the technical deep-dive was deferred. North America has lifecycle context and a captured catalogue description, but no completed technical walkthrough. A 669.477-second transcript gap prevents FULLY_GROUNDED status.

facts.fact: PGRegDoc.com is described as a custom backend hosted on P&G Azure, using SQL and a mail subscription service.
The application shares public, non-confidential safety data sheets and technical documents with consumers and customers through an external website.
The speaker says this document-sharing capability supports business requirements associated with REACH.
The speaker says they are not familiar with REACH and offers 'regulations' as their own informal meaning; this definition is not independently confirmed.
The application supports subscriptions and email notifications for updates about available documentation.

Three user groups are described: consumers/customers, global administrators, and local administrators; global admins manage countries, subscriptions, notifications/text modules, while local admins manage products/categories.
The public website remains within support scope because its backend application is supported; the precise frontend ownership boundary is not stated.
Admin employees manually add, edit, and delete country-specific safety data sheets and extract documents as PDFs; consumers retrieve available PDFs.
Application developers use the browser to perform manual application configuration.
The application has production and development environments; Azure SQL is described as data storage, Azure Data Factory as processing, and private endpoints/virtual networks as network controls.
The application reference slide/transcript identifies owner Miguel Angel Moreno-Fernandez, public classification, and low overall BIA.
The application flow diagram labels PingID as the authentication dependency; IT Access is named for user management. The exact spoken provider phrase remains unclear.
conflicts: Transcript exports render the spoken provider phrase differently; frame V-002 visibly labels PingID.

applications.application: North America Central Product Research Testing Panelist Payments

facts.fact: The application catalogue screen describes a Microsoft-run SaaS/ETL platform for North America CPRT panelist payment data and fulfilment data.
The catalogue description says Salesforce LEX data is exported and loaded to fulfilment vendor servers or a P&G-hosted database.
The catalogue description limits direct database access to PG NA CPRT business, technology development, and operations, with access needed for about five to six people at most.
The catalogue record shows lifecycle status Leverage/Optimize; the speaker says it moved from sunset to leverage optimized while decommissioning remained undecided.
Limited usage is reported from ticket history, and limited user count is explicitly presented as the speaker's impression.
Future requests for full decommissioning are expected; the recording does not say decommissioning was approved.
The speaker says code/scripts are stored in a place transcribed as 'data floor'; the proper platform name and location are not verified.
The presenter reports lacking permission to the application's Azure resource group; another participant advises trying an AMS Admin identity, but successful access is not shown.
The planned technical walkthrough was deferred; the presenter lacked preparation and access to resources/code.
The phrase 'transition to corruption mining' appears in the transcript during lifecycle discussion and cannot be safely interpreted from the available evidence.
